Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Combining two company internships > Second company placement after six company weeks
#### Second company placement after six company weeks

**Question/topic:** After a six-week company placement, how long must a second company internship be?

**Answer:** After a six-week company placement, a second company internship must last at least four weeks, with or without another summer course. This gives at least ten company weeks for this route. The complete arrangement requires prior written approval or petition, documentation and technical relevance. This rule describes the six-company-week plus second-company route; it does not change the standard eight-week minimum for a single approved placement or the separate approved six-plus-two faculty-research route.

## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Six company weeks alone
### Six company weeks alone

**Question/topic:** Are six company internship weeks alone enough for EECE 500?

**Answer:** No. The standard Approved Experience minimum is eight full weeks of approved training. For ECE, one documented way to complete a six-week company placement is two weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member; the company and research components must be approved and documented. If the completion route is a second company internship, that second placement must last at least four weeks, whether or not the student takes another summer course.

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > 6+2 arrangement definition
### 6+2 arrangement definition

**Question/topic:** How does a six-week internship plus two-week research arrangement work?

**Answer:** The six company weeks and two faculty-research weeks (2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member) must be approved and documented. Submit a separate research report in addition to the company internship report for the approved research component. Dar Al-Handasah is an example of a company offering six-week placements, not the only company eligible for a department-approved arrangement.

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Combining two company internships
### Combining two company internships

**Question/topic:** Can two company internships be combined for EECE500?

**Answer:** A combined arrangement requires prior written approval or petition. Each internship must be documented and technically relevant, and the total approved duration must satisfy EECE500 requirements. Meeting a duration total does not itself approve a particular split. Use the second-internship forms when instructed. The following scoped rules describe particular arrangements; apply their conditions to the proposed plan.

## Internship dates and duration changes

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can an internship be longer than eight weeks?

**Answer:** Yes. An approved internship may be longer than eight weeks. The Proposal, Notice of Arrival, and final employer letter should show the correct dates.

**Question/topic:** My internship end date is not fixed.

**Answer:** Enter the best date currently confirmed by the employer. When the date is finalized or changes, inform the coordinator and update or resubmit the relevant Moodle form if requested. The final employer letter must show the actual start and end dates.

   Do not silently transfer its numbers or requirements to an ordinary case.

   conditional outcomes and ask one short clarifying question. Do not lead with an
   unconditional Yes or No. If a brief follow-up could refer to several documented
   approval stages or deadlines, give the relevant rule or relative timing and ask

## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > Six company weeks alone

**Question/topic:** Are six company internship weeks alone enough for EECE 500?

**Answer:** No. The standard Approved Experience minimum is eight full weeks of approved training. For ECE, one documented way to complete a six-week company placement is two weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member; the company and research components must be approved and documented. If the completion route is a second company internship, that second placement must last at least four weeks, whether or not the student takes another summer course.

**Question/topic:** How does a six-week internship plus two-week research arrangement work?

**Answer:** The six company weeks and two faculty-research weeks (2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member) must be approved and documented. Submit a separate research report in addition to the company internship report for the approved research component. Dar Al-Handasah is an example of a company offering six-week placements, not the only company eligible for a department-approved arrangement.

**Question/topic:** What should the Progress Report cover for an approved six-week company internship plus two-week research arrangement?

Submit a separate research report for the approved research component, in addition to the company internship Final Report. These reporting rules apply to all departments with an approved arrangement, whether the company is Dar Al-Handasah or another company.

#### Second company placement after six company weeks

**Question/topic:** After a six-week company placement, how long must a second company internship be?

**Answer:** After a six-week company placement, a second company internship must last at least four weeks, with or without another summer course. This gives at least ten company weeks for this route. The complete arrangement requires prior written approval or petition, documentation and technical relevance. This rule describes the six-company-week plus second-company route; it does not change the standard eight-week minimum for a single approved placement or the separate approved six-plus-two faculty-research route.

### Six company weeks alone

**Question/topic:** Are six company internship weeks alone enough for EECE 500?

**Answer:** No. The standard Approved Experience minimum is eight full weeks of approved training. For ECE, one documented way to complete a six-week company placement is two weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member; the company and research components must be approved and documented. If the completion route is a second company internship, that second placement must last at least four weeks, whether or not the student takes another summer course.

## Taking another summer course

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. Students in any department may have to complete at least ten weeks of approved internship (ten weeks at one company or six weeks at one company plus four weeks at another) and schedule the other course before 8:30 AM or after 4:30 PM. Confirm whether these duration and class-time limits apply to your arrangement with the course team and current Moodle instructions before committing. They are not an unconditional ten-week requirement for every student taking another course. Separately, ECE and IEM students using a second company after a six-week placement must complete at least four weeks at that second company, whether or not they take another course.

Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > 6+2 arrangement definition
### 6+2 arrangement definition

**Question/topic:** How does a six-week internship plus two-week research arrangement work?

**Answer:** The six company weeks and two faculty-research weeks (2 weeks of research with an MSFEA faculty member) must be approved and documented. Submit a separate research report in addition to the company internship report for the approved research component. Dar Al-Handasah is an example of a company offering six-week placements, not the only company eligible for a department-approved arrangement.

**Answer:** Submit the Progress Report at the end of Week 4 of the company internship and cover only the company internship in that report.

## Internship dates and duration changes

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can an internship be longer than eight weeks?

**Department:** All departments

**Question/topic:** Can I take another summer course while completing my Approved Experience internship?

**Answer:** A concurrent summer course requires department, course-team, and employer approval, and the required internship work hours must still be completed. ## CO-OP overview

MSFEA CO-OP combines study with a full-time and paid work term of at least 6 months, associated with FEAA 500. It is an optional program. Apply to the program at least one year before your intended start. Eligibility requirements include a minimum GPA of 3.3 at application and course enrollment, at least 90 completed credits when enrolling in FEAA 500 (120 for architecture), and completion of the required career development modules before applying to positions and enrolling; departments may impose additional requirements. Students who pass FEAA 500 are no longer required to take their department's Approved Experience / Professional Training course. The application stages, conditions, tuition, work responsibilities and deliverables are explained below.

chunks.text:
## What CO-OP is

Cooperative education ("co-op") is a program in which students combine their
studies with one or more official **paid** work terms within their area of
study. The difference between a co-op work term and an internship is duration and
pay: internships are typically short (one or two months) and can be unpaid, while
co-op terms are longer and are paid. This is a general internship description;
the MSFEA Approved Experience internship course requires at least **8 weeks** of
approved training (see the course comparison below and the Summer Training Guidelines).
The **MSFEA co-op work term is a minimum of
6 months**, full-time and paid.

The department's Approved Experience internship is a graduation requirement. It
requires at least **8 weeks** of approved training and can be unpaid (see the

Guidelines.

Topic: MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course
### The FEAA 500 course

A student who accepts an offer enrolls in **FEAA 500 in both semesters** of the
co-op position (Summer and Fall, or Spring and Summer):

- **First semester:** register **FEAA 500** (3 credits) and pay its tuition.
- **Second semester:** register **FEAA 500A** (3 credits) with **no additional tuition** (no additional tuition fees).

Full-time student status is maintained in both semesters. A student with
satisfactory performance at the end of the first co-op semester receives a grade
of **"In Progress (PR)"** on FEAA 500; the final **Pass or Fail** grade is
assigned on **FEAA 500A** at the end of the second semester.

  undergraduate students (and to graduate students if allowed by their
  department).
- **Hours and salary:** students work **paid full-time jobs**, a minimum of 35–40
  hours per week. Pay should be higher than a stipend but slightly below a
  fresh-graduate salary. MSFEA can provide salary guidelines, but the salary is
  set by the employer.

- **Courses while on co-op:** enrolling in other courses during a co-op is **not

- **Number of credits:** the co-op is a **3-credit Pass/Fail FEAA 500** course.

## CO-OP overview

MSFEA CO-OP combines study with a full-time and paid work term of at least 6 months, associated with FEAA 500. It is an optional program. Apply to the program at least one year before your intended start. Eligibility requirements include a minimum GPA of 3.3 at application and course enrollment, at least 90 completed credits when enrolling in FEAA 500 (120 for architecture), and completion of the required career development modules before applying to positions and enrolling; departments may impose additional requirements. Students who pass FEAA 500 are no longer required to take their department's Approved Experience / Professional Training course. The application stages, conditions, tuition, work responsibilities and deliverables are explained below.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > What CO-OP is]
## What CO-OP is

Cooperative education ("co-op") is a program in which students combine their
studies with one or more official **paid** work terms within their area of
study. The difference between a co-op work term and an internship is duration and
pay: internships are typically short (one or two months) and can be unpaid, while
co-op terms are longer and are paid. This is a general internship description;
the MSFEA Approved Experience internship course requires at least **8 weeks** of
approved training (see the course comparison below and the Summer Training Guidelines).
The **MSFEA co-op work term is a minimum of
6 months**, full-time and paid.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > What CO-OP is]
## What CO-OP is

According to the U.S. Department of Education, students with co-op experience earn
almost 8–9% more within ten years of graduation compared to students with a
graduate degree.

> **Note on duration wording:** the general definition of co-op describes "at
> least four months" as a typical co-op length, but the **MSFEA requirement is a
> minimum of 6 months**. The 6-month figure is the one that applies to MSFEA
> students.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Number, duration, and certification:** one placement of at least 6 months is
  required; additional co-ops (consecutive or not) are allowed if approved by the
  department and co-op advisor. A 6-month co-op should typically coincide with the
  **Summer + Fall** or **Spring + Summer** semesters. The co-op appears as a
  course on the academic transcript.
- **Timing and return to campus:** the co-op should take place in the **3rd or 4th
  year** for engineering and graphic design students, and the **4th or 5th year**
  for architecture students. Students must **return to campus for at least one
  term** after their final co-op before graduating.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Approved Experience internship and CO-OP comparison]
## Approved Experience internship and CO-OP comparison

The department's Approved Experience internship is a graduation requirement. It
requires at least **8 weeks** of approved training and can be unpaid (see the
Summer Training Guidelines). MSFEA
CO-OP is an optional, full-time paid work term of at least **6 months**. Students
who pass FEAA 500 are no longer required to take their department's Approved
Experience / Professional Training course. The CO-OP rules and substitution are
specified in this handbook; the internship minimum comes from the Summer Training
Guidelines.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for employers > Position requirements]
Topic: MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for employers > Position requirements
### Position requirements

Co-op positions offered to MSFEA students should satisfy:

1. An established company known for meaningful training experiences.
2. A history of relationship with AUB and MSFEA (preferred).
3. Quality and relevance of the experience, evaluated by the co-op advisors from a
   detailed job description.
4. **Paid positions** — higher than a stipend and slightly below a full-time
   fresh-graduate salary.
5. Duration of **35–40 hours per week for 6 months**.

[email-clarifications.md > Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > 4+4 company-internship split]
Topic: Approved Internship Email Clarifications > Combined internship arrangements (ECE) > 4+4 company-internship split
### 4+4 company-internship split

**Question/topic:** Can EECE500 be split into two four-week internships?

**Answer:** Do not assume a 4+4 split is accepted. It is case-specific and requires a formal petition and written approval before either component is counted.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course]
Topic: MSFEA CO-OP (Cooperative Education) Handbook > Information for students > The FEAA 500 course
### The FEAA 500 course

A student who accepts an offer enrolls in **FEAA 500 in both semesters** of the
co-op position (Summer and Fall, or Spring and Summer):

- **First semester:** register **FEAA 500** (3 credits) and pay its tuition.
- **Second semester:** register **FEAA 500A** (3 credits) with **no additional tuition** (no additional tuition fees).

Full-time student status is maintained in both semesters. A student with
satisfactory performance at the end of the first co-op semester receives a grade
of **"In Progress (PR)"** on FEAA 500; the final **Pass or Fail** grade is
assigned on **FEAA 500A** at the end of the second semester.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies

- **Optional or required:** CO-OP is an **optional program**, open to
  undergraduate students (and to graduate students if allowed by their
  department).
- **Hours and salary:** students work **paid full-time jobs**, a minimum of 35–40
  hours per week. Pay should be higher than a stipend but slightly below a
  fresh-graduate salary. MSFEA can provide salary guidelines, but the salary is
  set by the employer.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Courses while on co-op:** enrolling in other courses during a co-op is **not
  allowed**, with a possible exception for a Final Year Project (FYP) or
  research-based course (499) if the department allows it and the co-op academic
  advisor (and FYP group members, for an FYP) approve — and only if it does not
  interfere with working hours.
- **Number of credits:** the co-op is a **3-credit Pass/Fail FEAA 500** course.
  Whether it counts toward academic credit, and whether it is treated as a free
  elective or a technical elective, is decided by each department. Students keep
  **full-time student status** during the co-op.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Tuition / co-op fees:** regular tuition is charged for the 3 credits of FEAA
  500.
- **Approved Experience substitution:** students who pass FEAA 500 are **no longer
  required** to take the Approved Experience / Professional Training course in
  their department (that course is currently billed as 1 credit). Its current course-credit and billing information is maintained
  in the approved internship course clarification, separately from CO-OP tuition.

[msfea-cdc-coop-handbook.md > Policies]
## Policies
- **Preparation and support:** info sessions, co-op advising weeks, on-demand
  meetings with the co-op CDC Advisor (resume review, counseling, mock
  interviews), the career development modules, access to co-op employers and
  opportunities, follow-up and feedback, and faculty mentorship and assessment.
- **Program length and graduation date:** students may take overloads to complete
  the co-op without delaying graduation, with careful planning and department
  approval. In some cases participation may delay graduation by one term (for one
  co-op).
